title: Unit 1: Study Skills - Key Vocabulary & Terminology

content.meaning_en: Lasting for a very short time; temporary.
content.example_sentence: Spoken language is transient, so taking notes during a lecture is essential.

content.meaning_en: Things that prevent someone from giving full attention.
content.example_sentence: Sit near the front of the room to avoid environmental distractions.

content.meaning_en: In exactly the same words as were used originally.
content.example_sentence: Do not try to write down the lecture verbatim; focus on main ideas.

content.meaning_en: Signals or hints given by a speaker to indicate key points.
content.example_sentence: Good students listen for vocal cues from the lecturer to identify important topics.

content.meaning_en: Having or showing refined judgment; selective.
content.example_sentence: Effective note-taking requires being a discriminating listener.

content.meaning_en: Extremely useful; priceless.
content.example_sentence: Reading provides invaluable knowledge for your future career.

content.meaning_en: Read quickly to get the general idea or gist.
content.example_sentence: I skimmed through the chapter to understand the main topic before class.

content.meaning_en: Look through text quickly to locate a specific piece of information.
content.example_sentence: Scan the table of contents to find where the vocabulary section is located.

content.meaning_en: Take in and fully understand information or ideas.
content.example_sentence: Students read academic books to assimilate new concepts into their understanding.

content.meaning_en: A stock of skills, techniques, or devices used in a particular field.
content.example_sentence: University students should use their entire repertoire of reading skills.

content.meaning_en: Hasty and therefore not thorough or detailed.
content.example_sentence: A newspaper often gives only a cursory coverage of complex events.

content.meaning_en: Available for one's use whenever desired.
content.example_sentence: Students have various learning strategies at their disposal.

content.meaning_en: Essential tools or crucial factors that provide access to understanding.
content.example_sentence: Reading skills are the keys to unlocking complex academic knowledge.

content.meaning_en: The opportunity or means to enter, approach, or retrieve information.
content.example_sentence: Students need easy access to diverse library reference materials.

content.meaning_en: The ways in which something is regarded, understood, or interpreted.
content.example_sentence: Academic reading helps broaden a student's perceptions of world issues.

content.meaning_en: Explained, understood, or analyzed in a specified way.
content.example_sentence: The survey results were interpreted using statistical analysis.

content.meaning_en: Looking at or reading something very quickly without paying attention to detail.
content.example_sentence: He was glancing through the daily paper while waiting for the lecture.

content.meaning_en: To remove, derive, or select specific facts or main points from a text.
content.example_sentence: Effective note-takers extract only the essential points from the presentation.

content.meaning_en: To change or differ according to the circumstances or purpose.
content.example_sentence: Your reading speed should vary based on the difficulty of the passage.

content.meaning_en: The main ideas, subjects, or underlying topics in a text or lecture.
content.example_sentence: The professor outlined the central themes of the course during the orientation.

content.meaning_en: Identifying or acknowledging words, concepts, or details previously learned.
content.example_sentence: Reading is about understanding context, not just recognizing individual words.
